title: Police now using scrapped Clean Air Zone cameras to catch criminals

evidence_packet.title: Police now using scrapped Clean Air Zone cameras to catch criminals
evidence_packet.lead: A public consultation backed the transfer to police, but respondents also raised concerns about privacy
evidence_packet.summary: A public consultation backed the transfer to police, but respondents also raised concerns about privacy
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Police have been catching criminals by using cameras installed as part of an abandoned Clean Air Zone scheme Greater Manchester Police (GMP) took control of about 400 automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) cameras that were supposed to be used to enforce the planned region-wide low-emission zone And they have been used to make "multiple arrests", a senior officer said The cameras were installed as part of Greater Manchester's drive to cut the number of high-emission vehicles on the regions roads, but the plans were dropped in favour of other efforts to make the region's transport network more environmentally friendly Deputy chief constable Terry Woods told Greater Manchester's police, fire and crime panel on Monday the system was making a significant difference "It's been tangible, multiple arrests on the back of that system and it's keeping people safe," he said

title: Oldham library shut for emergency work as asbestos found in floor

evidence_packet.title: Oldham library shut for emergency work as asbestos found in floor
evidence_packet.lead: It comes after the library was closed earlier this year when staff reported 'bouncy' floors
evidence_packet.summary: It comes after the library was closed earlier this year when staff reported 'bouncy' floors
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham library shut for emergency work as asbestos found in floor - BBC News Image source, Oldham Council Image caption, Asbestos was discovered after 'bouncy' floors triggered an investigation at Royton Library, in Oldham By Ed Barnes Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 1 hour ago A library has been closed for urgent repairs after asbestos and contaminated debris were discovered beneath its floors. Royton Library, in Oldham, closed earlier this year after staff reported sections of flooring had become "bouncy" and inspectors found severe dry rot. Further investigations uncovered asbestos, a hazardous material once widely used in construction, beneath the building's floors the Local Democracy Reporting Service reported . According to a council report, the work is expected to take five to six weeks and is needed to address "immediate health, safety and building risks". Councillors are due to consider the plans on 19 November. Image source, Oldham Council Image caption, It comes after the library was refurbished as part of a £4m scheme which finished in 2024 The total costs of the work is not currently known and any potential costs have not been made public, according to the LDRS. The library will operate from Downey House on Church Street, in Royton, until further notice. Subnum Hariff-Khan, Oldham Council's head of heritage, libraries and arts, said in October: "We know how important Royton Library is to local residents and we're pleased to be able to continue delivering a library service while these essential repairs take place." "We'd like to thank customers for their patience and understanding while these essential works are carried out to secure the future of this important library building." title: 'Predatory' Wigan doctor should have been barred, High Court rules

evidence_packet.title: 'Predatory' Wigan doctor should have been barred, High Court rules
evidence_packet.lead: A decision to suspend a doctor for 12 months has been overruled by a judge on appeal
evidence_packet.summary: A decision to suspend a doctor for 12 months has been overruled by a judge on appeal
evidence_packet.evidence_text: 'Predatory' Wigan doctor should have been barred, High Court rules - BBC News Image source, Google Image caption, The incidents occurred at the A&E department of the Royal Albert Edward Infirmary, in Wigan, the tribunal heard By Hannah Richardson Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 17 November 2026 A "predatory" doctor should have been struck off for carrying out "sexually motivated examinations" of junior colleagues, a High Court judge has ruled. Dr Khush Bakhat Muhammad Zeeshan was suspended for 12 months by the Medical Practitioners Tribunal Service over incidents at the Royal Albert Infirmary. It took into account that he had not committed the misconduct again, and that some colleagues spoke in his favour. But in overturning the tribunal's decision, Mr Justice Squires said the fact that Zeeshan "had not repeated the misconduct while under active investigation cold not be sufficient" to avoid being barred from the profession. The tribunal found Zeeshan had "exploited the health concerns of two female junior colleagues", touching them on their breasts and bottom, which it said amounted to "serious misconduct". He denied the allegations, which meant he had had "not been able to demonstrate significant insight" into his misconduct, the panel found. It could not "fully assess" the risk that he might do it again, it said. But the panel noted that by the time it was deciding how to punish him, it was five years since the incidents happened. It decided to suspend him for a year "to allow him the opportunity to show that he had developed insight into the concern identified". title: Aspiring electrician applies in vain for 100-plus apprenticeships

evidence_packet.title: Aspiring electrician applies in vain for 100-plus apprenticeships
evidence_packet.lead: Dawud Hussain, 18, is studying to become an electrician but has yet to secure an apprenticeship
evidence_packet.summary: Dawud Hussain, 18, is studying to become an electrician but has yet to secure an apprenticeship
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Aspiring electrician applies in vain for 100-plus apprenticeships - BBC News Image caption, Dawud Hussain says he has struggled to find an apprenticeship as an electrician By Haider Saleem , North West and Liv Cleal , Reporting from Altrincham, Greater Manchester Published 17 November 2026 A teenager who wants to become an electrician said he had applied for more than 100 apprenticeships without any success. Dawud Hussain, who is studying electrical installation at Tameside College in Greater Manchester, and also works in a barbershop, said most employers did not even respond to his applications. The 18-year-old spoke to BBC Radio Manchester as a major government-commissioned review set out recommendations for reducing the number of Neets (young people who are not in education, employment or training). City region mayor Bev Craig wants more powers to tackle youth unemployment, including plans for a new apprenticeships hub to double the number available. Dawud, who is seeking an apprenticeship starting in September 2027, said that while his college course was going well, finding an opportunity outside the classroom was proving to be very difficult. "It's like you don't get a chance," he said. "It's tough, it's really tough because when you apply for so much and you don't get a reply back..." He said only a couple of employers had spoken to him, while others either rejected his applications or failed to respond. Dawud said he had been working at a barbershop for about two years but "my first choice is being an electrician". Although he is studying and working, Dawud's difficulties securing an apprenticeship illustrate wider concerns about the number of Neets. title: Hundreds of properties hit by power cuts after cable incidents

evidence_packet.title: Hundreds of properties hit by power cuts after cable incidents
evidence_packet.lead: Hundreds of customers in Greater Manchester and Lancashire remain without electricity
evidence_packet.summary: Hundreds of customers in Greater Manchester and Lancashire remain without electricity
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Hundreds of properties hit by power cuts after cable incidents - BBC News Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Properties across Greater Manchester and Lancashire are without power By Angela Ferguson North West Published 17 November 2026 Hundreds of properties in Greater Manchester and Lancashire have been hit by power cuts caused by "unexpected" incidents including underground cables. SP Electricity North West (SPENW) said properties in Oldham, Rochdale, Salford, Blackpool, Lancaster, Myerscough and Bilsborrow and North Meols had been affected. SPENW apologised for the disruption, saying that about 279 properties in Myerscough and Bilsborrow in Lancashire had since been reconnected. "Our engineers are working as quickly and safely as possible to restore supplies," said a spokesperson. In Saddleworth, Oldham, 191 properties continue to be affected, with SPENW preparing to send a team out to investigate. In Cadishead and Lower Irlam in Salford, 126 properties are without electricity, with engineers already on site. In the Clifton area of Blackpool, 60 properties are cut off, with engineers en route. In Whalley in the Ribble Valley, 244 properties remain cut off. And in North Meols in West Lancashire, 119 properties are affected, with SPENW preparing to send a crew out. A spokesperson said: "We are aware of separate power cuts affecting properties in parts of Lancashire and Greater Manchester due to faults on the underground electricity network. "Our engineers are working as quickly and safely as possible to restore supplies, and we apologise for the disruption caused." evidence_packet.title: Altrincham hotel to stop housing asylum seekers, MP says
evidence_packet.lead: Conor Rand says Cresta Court Hotel in Altrincham will "end housing asylum seekers" within months
evidence_packet.summary: Conor Rand says Cresta Court Hotel in Altrincham will "end housing asylum seekers" within months
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Altrincham hotel to stop housing asylum seekers, MP says - BBC News Image caption, Cresta Court Hotel in Altrincham has been used to house male asylum seekers since November 2024 By Kevin Fitzpatrick , Greater Manchester political reporter and Rachael Lazaro , North West Published 17 November 2026 A hotel that has been the scene of anti-immigration demonstrations and counter-protests over the last two years will stop housing asylum seekers, the local MP has said. Labour's Conor Rand confirmed the 148-bedroom Cresta Court in Altrincham, Greater Manchester, would "end housing asylum seekers within the next three months as the remaining residents are moved out of the hotel". The local Conservative group claimed the decision came off the back of its "two years of relentless campaigning". A spokesperson for the Home Office said the closure was part of its policy of "closing every asylum hotel and moving asylum seekers into alternative accommodation, including former military sites". Several protests have taken place outside Cresta Court since it began being used to house asylum seekers in 2024, attracting a large police presence. Image source, Reuters Image caption, Anti-immigration protesters gathered outside the hotel in August last year Rand told BBC Radio Manchester : "Hotels are not suitable places to house asylum seekers. "It's bad news for community, bad news for taxpayers, and bad news for people themselves seeking asylum. "It's a practice that should never have been started." Image caption, Labour MP Conor Rand says hotels are "not suitable" places to house asylum seekers In 2023, at the peak of the policy of housing asylum seekers in hotels, 400 were in use at a cost of £9m a day, according to the government. title: Demolition of Rochdale's Seven Sisters flats devastating, residents say

evidence_packet.title: Demolition of Rochdale's Seven Sisters flats devastating, residents say
evidence_packet.lead: Residents who have been informed that their flats will be bulldozed say they will continue to "fight"
evidence_packet.summary: Residents who have been informed that their flats will be bulldozed say they will continue to "fight"
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Demolition of Rochdale's Seven Sisters flats devastating, residents say - BBC News Image caption, Christina Hartley and Roy Kitcher say the flats are "home" and they do not want to move By Davinia Ramos , Reporting from in Rochdale and Rebecca Brahde , North West Published 17 November 2026 Residents of a town's tower blocks which are set to be demolished have said it is "devastating" but they will continue to "fight" the decision. Rochdale's Seven Sisters tower blocks, which contain 766 flats, will be replaced by about 600 homes , social landlord Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) has said. Demolition of the tower blocks was first proposed in 2017 but was ruled out in 2023 after a local campaign against it, but residents began moving out in October 2025 over long-term safety concerns. Roy Kitcher and Christina Hartley, who have lived in one of the blocks for 14 years, said they were left "upset" and "angry". RBH said demolition was the only "realistic and affordable" option. Kitcher said: "It's devastating news - why they want to knock them down, I don't know." The couple are one of 78 households yet to accept an offer of another home. "This is home and I want to stay here, I don't want to be moving out again," Kitcher added. Hartley said: "I'm just so upset about it and angry." She said the council had asked her to look at accommodation, however it was not in the town. "I want to stay in Rochdale, I'm a Rochdale girl born and bred and I won't move until they find me somewhere round here," she said. Image source, Reuters Image caption, The seven sisters in Rochdale were built in the 1960s A local campaign, previously backed by Rochdale Council, had appealed for the buildings to be refurbished rather than demolished. title: 'Predatory' Wigan doctor should have been barred, High Court rules

evidence_packet.title: 'Predatory' Wigan doctor should have been barred, High Court rules
evidence_packet.lead: A "predatory" doctor should have been struck off for carrying out "sexually motivated examinations" of junior colleagues, a High Court judge has ruled Dr Khush Bakhat Muhammad Zeeshan was suspended for 12 months by the Medical Practitioners Tribunal Service over incidents at the
evidence_packet.summary: A "predatory" doctor should have been struck off for carrying out "sexually motivated examinations" of junior colleagues, a High Court judge has ruled Dr Khush Bakhat Muhammad Zeeshan was suspended for 12 months by the Medical Practitioners Tribunal Service over incidents at the
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A "predatory" doctor should have been struck off for carrying out "sexually motivated examinations" of junior colleagues, a High Court judge has ruled Dr Khush Bakhat Muhammad Zeeshan was suspended for 12 months by the Medical Practitioners Tribunal Service over incidents at the Royal Albert Infirmary It took into account that he had not committed the misconduct again, and that some colleagues spoke in his favour But in overturning the tribunal's decision, Mr Justice Squires said the fact that Zeeshan "had not repeated the misconduct while under active investigation cold not be sufficient" to avoid being barred from the profession The tribunal found Zeeshan had "exploited the health concerns of two female junior colleagues", touching them on their breasts and bottom, which it said amounted to "serious misconduct" He denied the allegations, which meant he had had "not been able to demonstrate significant insight" into his misconduct, the panel found

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Residents of a town's tower blocks which are set to be demolished have said it is "devastating" but they will continue to "fight" the decision Rochdale's Seven Sisters tower blocks, which contain 766 flats, will be replaced by about 600 homes , social landlord Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) has said Demolition of the tower blocks was first proposed in 2017 but was ruled out in 2023 after a local campaign against it, but residents began moving out in October 2025 over long-term safety concerns Roy Kitcher and Christina Hartley, who have lived in one of the blocks for 14 years, said they were left "upset" and "angry". RBH said demolition was the only "realistic and affordable" option Kitcher said: "It's devastating news - why they want to knock them down, I don't know." The couple are one of 78 households yet to accept an offer of another home

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Large outdoor concerts are due to return to Manchester's Platt Fields Park next summer, with LCD Soundsystem named as the first headliner The American rock band will perform at the park in Fallowfield on 30 July 2027, with Young Fathers, Cowboy Hunters and DJs Erol Alkan and Luka Una also on the bill Organisers said the concert would be part of a series of shows, each with a capacity of 25,000, taking place over two weekends in late July and early August The events, called PlattForm, are being organised by The Warehouse Project, SJM Concerts and Live Nation, with more artists due to be announced in the coming weeks Platt Fields Park previously hosted the Parklife music festival from 2010 to 2012, before it moved to Heaton Park in 2013 to accommodate growing crowds Other music festivals have since taken place at the park, including Flashback Festival in 2022 and 2023

evidence_packet.evidence_text: NHS leaders in the north-west of England have urged people to take steps to protect their health as forecasters warn of snow A yellow warning for wintry weather in Greater Manchester and Lancashire came into force at midnight and will apply until 11:00 GMT Meanwhile the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has issued a "yellow cold-health alert" covering three regions - the North West, North East and Yorkshire and the Humber - which will be place until 09:00 on Thursday The agency explained that the cold conditions could result in increased demand for healthcare services and a greater risk to life for vulnerable people Paula Cowan, the UKHSA's regional director for primary care, communities and neighbourhood, said: "Winter is always the toughest time of the year for the NHS "The public can play their part by taking simple measures to stay well this winter, such as getting winter vaccines when invited to, keeping warm, staying active, looking out for others, and choosing the right service when they need help," she continued

Town hall bosses will receive £2.5m from the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) to test what is called the ‘Place Based Regeneration Pilot’ The idea behind this pilot is to bring work to build new homes; retrofit current housing; and environmental improvements under one roof It is hoped that this collaborative approach between public bodies could help speed up development and reduce costs compared to projects being brought forward individually. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport ASDA pulls out of controversial plan which attracted 'most objections in Stockport history' “We look forward to seeing the store delivered in due course, providing more shopping choices for local people" Add to preferred sources Comments New Supermarket chain ASDA has confirmed they have pulled out of a controversial project in Stockport after it was given the green light by planners Earlier this year, Stockport council rejected plans to demolish a car repair garage and MOT test centre and replace it with a new shop at 22 Marple Road in Offerton. The plans made reference to the new unit being occupied by ASDA Express, but were developer-led The plans came up against significant opposition from people in the area with a letter of objection signed by 1,800 people and 1,272 individual comments submitted on Stockport council’s planning portal. The biggest concern was the new shop’s impact on local independent businesses Town hall bosses later rejected the plans arguing the plans did not show ‘the proposed retail use could be properly and safely serviced without causing a detrimental impact on highway safety and parking’. 13 car parking spaces are included in the plans However Aim Capital Ltd appealed the local authority’s decision. Earlier this week, planning inspector Katie McDonald overruled Stockport council and gave the greenlight for the development to go ahead

He was killed in the incident, jurors in a trial at Manchester Crown Court were told yesterday (November 17) The driver of the truck, Michael Yates, 58, of Kirkfell Walk in Oldham , denies causing Mr Al-Ghamdi's death. Prosecutor Niamh McGinty told jurors in her opening of the case that the collision took place just before mid-day Mr Yates had been driving a flat-bed truck eastwards after turning left off Deansgate , and was delivering some equipment to a building site. Mr Al-Ghamdi was travelling along the same road behind Mr Yates, Ms McGinty said, riding a bike in the cycle lane to the left of the truck Upon approaching the junction with Watson Street, where the lights were red, Mr Yates slowed down, while Mr Al-Ghamdi continued in the cycle lane towards the rear of the vehicle

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts The 'accident waiting to happen' that cost a devoted dad, 42, his life John Graveson was killed instantly at his work in Tameside John Graveson died in March 2023 (Image: Family handout) Add to preferred sources News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 05:51, 18 Nov 2026 When John Graveson waved goodbye to his family three years ago, he had every reason to believe he would return home that evening The 42-year-old went to work on the morning of March 3, 2023, as he had done countless times before, expecting to come home to his partner Shelly and their daughter. His daughter continues to grow, reaching milestones without her dad by her side And now, a jury has found that the circumstances which led to Mr Graveson's death were entirely preventable, finding the waste management company he worked for guilty of corporate manslaughter Mr Graveson was employed as a picker at AMP NW Ltd - now Waste Solutions Mcr Ltd - at Aspire House industrial estate in Dukinfield, Tameside

An extraordinary place scrutiny council meeting heard that the extra cash has been allocated from the Greater Manchester Mayor’s pothole fund to be spend on resurfacing in the borough In a presentation the committee, Dwayne Lowe, a non-political deputy director the council, said the funding would be split in varying amounts across all 20 wards of Bolton . He said where the money would be spent was determined by a ‘data led and risk-based approach’, which selec He added that surveys done by the highways departments pick up condition data including potholes, surface deflection (rutting), cracking and fretting, texture loss, defective iron work and the skid resistance of the road surface He said other considerations included the amount of traffic, bus routes and the vicinity of schools and hospitals and that which wards the roads which needed the work were in was not considered in the process The breakdown by ward showed that £1.366m of the funding would be spent in the Breightmet, the largest amount. The next two highest wards by spend will be Farnworth North with £908,000 allocated and Queens Park and Central with £624,000

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Ashton and Mossley The town that could set the ‘blueprint’ for the rest of Greater Manchester The regeneration of Ashton-under-Lyne could soon be used as a model for the rest of Greater Manchester to follow Add to preferred sources Comments News Georg There’s something going on in Ashton, and it could become a ‘blueprint’ for the rest of Greater Manchester The Tameside town has been chosen to pilot a new way of integrating affordable house building and wider area improvements. Town hall bosses will receive £2.5m from the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) to test what is called the ‘Place Based Regeneration Pilot’ The idea behind this pilot is to bring work to build new homes; retrofit current housing; and environmental improvements under one roof It is hoped that this collaborative approach between public bodies could help speed up development and reduce costs compared to projects being brought forward individually. If successful, the same methods could be used in regeneration projects across the city-region Deputy mayor for Greater Manchester, Paul Dennett, told the latest GMCA meeting: “This will set a blueprint for how we do regeneration across the region.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport ASDA pulls out of controversial plan which attracted 'most objections in Stockport history' “We look forward to seeing the store delivered in due course, providing more shopping choices for local people" Add to preferred sources Comments New Supermarket chain ASDA has confirmed they have pulled out of a controversial project in Stockport after it was given the green light by planners Earlier this year, Stockport council rejected plans to demolish a car repair garage and MOT test centre and replace it with a new shop at 22 Marple Road in Offerton. The plans made reference to the new unit being occupied by ASDA Express, but were developer-led The plans came up against significant opposition from people in the area with a letter of objection signed by 1,800 people and 1,272 individual comments submitted on Stockport council’s planning portal. The biggest concern was the new shop’s impact on local independent businesses Town hall bosses later rejected the plans arguing the plans did not show ‘the proposed retail use could be properly and safely serviced without causing a detrimental impact on highway safety and parking’. 13 car parking spaces are included in the plans However Aim Capital Ltd appealed the local authority’s decision. Earlier this week, planning inspector Katie McDonald overruled Stockport council and gave the greenlight for the development to go ahead

evidence_packet.summary: Courts The 'accident waiting to happen' that cost a devoted dad, 42, his life John Graveson was killed instantly at his work in Tameside John Graveson died in March 2023 (Image: Family handout) Add to preferred sources News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 05:51, 18
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts The 'accident waiting to happen' that cost a devoted dad, 42, his life John Graveson was killed instantly at his work in Tameside John Graveson died in March 2023 (Image: Family handout) Add to preferred sources News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 05:51, 18 Nov 2026 When John Graveson waved goodbye to his family three years ago, he had every reason to believe he would return home that evening The 42-year-old went to work on the morning of March 3, 2023, as he had done countless times before, expecting to come home to his partner Shelly and their daughter. But on that day, an unthinkable incident occurred - and Mr Graveson never made it home His family are still living with the devastating consequences of a loss that has left an "incredibly vast" void in their lives. His daughter continues to grow, reaching milestones without her dad by her side And now, a jury has found that the circumstances which led to Mr Graveson's death were entirely preventable, finding the waste management company he worked for guilty of corporate manslaughter Mr Graveson was employed as a picker at AMP NW Ltd - now Waste Solutions Mcr Ltd - at Aspire House industrial estate in Dukinfield, Tameside

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A Company been found guilty of corporate manslaughter at Manchester Crown Court and Section 2 Health & Safety at Work Act offence after the death of an employee at skip hire yard in Dukinfield Anthony Elston aged 49 , Clifton – owner of AMP NW Ltd, has been found guilty of Section 2 Health & Safety at Work Act offence and John Horan aged Burnley, has been found guilty of Section 7 – Health & Safety at Work Act The court heard that on the morning of 3 March 2023, John Horan, a yard manager and machine operator employed by AMP NW Ltd, was operating a Hyundai HW140 excavator within the yard At the same time, 42-year-old John Graveson, who had worked at the site as a waste picker for approximately one year, was walking through the yard. John Graveson moved alongside the excavator before continuing behind it As John Graveson passed behind the excavator, Horan placed the vehicle into reverse and began manoeuvring backwards. Although the excavator’s reversing alarm was sounding and its blue warning lights were illuminated, Horan remained facing forwards and failed to observe John Grave The excavator struck John Graveson, and proceeded to crush him, causing catastrophic injuries from which he sadly died at the scene

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police (GMP) took control of about 400 automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) cameras that were supposed to be used to enforce the planned region-wide low-emission zone And they have been used to make "multiple arrests", a senior officer said The cameras were installed as part of Greater Manchester's drive to cut the number of high-emission vehicles on the regions roads, but the plans were dropped in favour of other efforts to make the region's transport network more environmentally friendly Deputy chief constable Terry Woods told Greater Manchester's police, fire and crime panel on Monday the system was making a significant difference "It's been tangible, multiple arrests on the back of that system and it's keeping people safe," he said Deputy Mayor Kate Green said: "They are not speed cameras, they are being used for crime detection and as an investigative tool."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Dr Khush Bakhat Muhammad Zeeshan was suspended for 12 months by the Medical Practitioners Tribunal Service over incidents at the Royal Albert Infirmary It took into account that he had not committed the misconduct again, and that some colleagues spoke in his favour But in overturning the tribunal's decision, Mr Justice Squires said the fact that Zeeshan "had not repeated the misconduct while under active investigation cold not be sufficient" to avoid being barred from the profession The tribunal found Zeeshan had "exploited the health concerns of two female junior colleagues", touching them on their breasts and bottom, which it said amounted to "serious misconduct" He denied the allegations, which meant he had had "not been able to demonstrate significant insight" into his misconduct, the panel found It could not "fully assess" the risk that he might do it again, it said

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A 27-year-old man was stabbed several times on Moss Bank in Crumpsall shortly after 01:30 GMT on Saturday and died in an ambulance from his injuries, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said The force said the victim had been attacked by "a number of males", all believed to have been wearing dark clothing and balaclavas A 26-year-old man is being questioned in police custody on suspicion of murder Detectives urged any witnesses or anyone with information about the stabbing to come forward Det Insp Neil Higginson said officers were "continuing to support the victim's family during this extremely difficult time" He said the investigation into the man's "tragic death" was continuing, adding: "I would urge anyone who witnessed the incident, saw the movements of vehicles, or has any information that could assist our investigation to contact us however insignificant you think it might be."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Construction Begins on Two New Game-Changing Sports Hubs for Wythenshawe Communities | Manchester City Council Construction Begins on Two New Game-Changing Sports Hubs for Wythenshawe Communities Tuesday 17 November 2026 Construction has begun at two major new Football Foundation multisport Hubs in Wythenshawe, marking a significant milestone in the transformation of community sport across South Manchester. The two new sites will help transform grassroots sport, improve health and wellbeing, and create new opportunities for thousands of local people. Backed by £11 million of investment from the Premier League, The FA and Government's Football Foundation, alongside Manchester City Council, the NHS and other local authority partners, the development at Wythenshawe Park and Wythenshawe Sports Ground will provide modern, inclusive and accessible facilities that support people of all ages and abilities to get active, connect with their communities and enjoy sport year-round. As construction got underway, partners celebrated the milestone with a special ‘spade-in-the-ground' event on 12 November 2026. The event was attended by representatives of all three Football Foundation partners: the Premier League, The FA and Government, as well as representatives of the Manchester County FA, the Mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig OBE, and local MP, Mike Kane. Wythenshawe Sports Ground Hub is a flagship women's and girls' site and will be the central venue for the South Manchester Girls' League once built. Wythenshawe Park Hub, meanwhile, will include a dedicated GP surgery, which will support an integrated approach to health and wellbeing in the community. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Children and families are set to benefit from improved play areas in Failsworth after Oldham Council secured £270,000 from the Government's Playground Fund The funding forms part of an £18million government programme to create or refurbish playgrounds in England's areas of greatest need over the next two years The government selected Failsworth to receive a share of the fund, with three play areas identified as eligible for investment through the programme for 66 local authorities Funding will be used to improve playground facilities and support community-led design and engagement activities, giving residents the opportunity to help shape the future of these spaces The three eligible sites are Higher Memorial Park which will receive £160,000, Daisy Nook Country Park which will receive £60,000 and Lower Memorial Park which has been allocated £50,000 A larger share will go to Higher Memorial Park because this has received significantly less external investment than the other locations in recent years

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

Hear the hidden history of the female pioneers who drank, distilled, and defied , while enjoying cocktails inspired by them Drinking history expert Simon Sharp takes you on a journey from the invention of the pub and modern beer, to distillation and champagne – where women have been at the forefront , challenging patriarchy so we can all enjoy a drink To illustrate these stories guests will enjoy four cocktails; The Mansplainer, The Poinsettia, Bees Knees, and Hanky Panky – all invented or inspired by these trailblazing ladies, crafted with ingredients sourced from female founded and led businesses A tribute to women’s creativity and courage , this tasting celebrates the mark they’ve left on drinking culture Simon Sharp is a history geek, drinks expert, and spirits judge. He travels around the country hosting tastings and talks revolving around the history of drinking. He has also appeared on radio, podcasts, and newspapers expressing his enthusiasm for drinking history and culture Are you more independent or community focused? Experimental or measured? evidence_packet.evidence_text: Get ready for a huge dose of boy band nostalgia as Boys Are Back Again hits venues across the UK Headlining the tour are the legendary East 17, one of the UK’s biggest ever boy bands and true trailblazers of the 90s pop era. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot and From the grill, guests can enjoy the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallot, alongside the slow-cooked Thai Lamb Shoulder, served with red thai sauce, chilli and coriander

evidence_packet.lead: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities.
evidence_packet.summary: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals

Its third movement, Ecstasio , is s Between these two pieces comes a world premiere: Gabriella Smith’s How To Be A Bird , written for tonight’s soloist Pekka Kuusisto. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester City Transfer News The £100m transfer reality Man City have to accept Jack Grealish is at a career crossroads but his time at Manchester City will come to an end in the summer Jack Grealish will leave Manchester City in the summer when his contract expir Add to preferred sources Comments Sport Alex James Content Editor 14:00, 17 Nov 2026 A little over three years ago, Jack Grealish was at the peak of his powers. A Champions League winner, a Premier League winner and an FA Cup winner after an incredible season with Manchester City Now the England international is at a significant crossroads. He's missed the last four matches with loan club Everton owing to a disciplinary breach and while he could return to action this weekend against Brentford his long-term future is uncertain The arrival of Enzo Maresca at the Etihad in the summer, someone with whom Grealish forged a close bond during the 2022-23 season when the Italian was on Pep Guardiola's coaching staff, was viewed by some as a potential olive branch for the 31-year-old Get all the best Man City news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the MEN! Grealish came off the bench for City in the opening day win over Bournemouth but re-joined Everton on loan shortly after and his Etihad career is expected to come to an end in the summer when his contract expires

evidence_packet.lead: Murat Dalkılıç at Indigo at The O2
evidence_packet.summary: Приготовьтесь к незабываемому вечеру с одной из самых любимых звезд турецкой поп-сцены — Муратом Далкылычем, в Лондоне! После выхода хита «Kasaba» в 2008 году Мурат Далкылыч стал одной из главных фигур турецкой поп-музыки
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Приготовьтесь к незабываемому вечеру с одной из самых любимых звезд турецкой поп-сцены — Муратом Далкылычем, в Лондоне! После выхода хита «Kasaba» в 2008 году Мурат Далкылыч стал одной из главных фигур турецкой поп-музыки. Он известен своим узнаваемым голосом, энергичными выступлениями и популярными песнями, среди которых «Bir Güzellik Yap».
